answer: Split each n-bit input into q = ceiling(n/b) digits in radix 2^b, where b = ceiling(log2 n). Their product is the wrap-around product (the wiki's totipuv) of the two digit sequences, padded to a length S that is a product of distinct odd primes with T/2 < S < T, and no wrap-around occurs because the padded length is large enough. The sequence is then reindexed onto prime-length axes by a fixed reindexing map (the Lolazad page). Each prime-length transform (the wiki's tobifup) is computed through a power-of-two transform, using a resampling identity with fixed linear contractions and phase multipliers (Sikusup and Divasov), with the permutations kept inside the identity so none is executed as a sort. The stages in order are: radix digits; reindexing onto prime axes; two forward transforms of the two sequences; pointwise product of the transforms; one opposite transform; rescaling by S and by 2^(2b+4)S; rounding each entry to the nearest integer; undoing the reindexing; and carry propagation in radix 2^b, which outputs exactly 2n bits. The result is exact rather than approximate because all values are kept to p = 6b fractional bits and the accumulated error on each coefficient is below 1/2; the true coefficients are integers, so rounding returns them exactly, and carry propagation then gives the exact binary product. I am not fully sure of the constants: the wiki's exactness bound is stated only for digit widths b at least 2^24, and I did not see why the prime-length detour is needed.

key_idea.statement: The exact product is the digit-sequence wrap-around product computed through transforms; each coefficient is off by less than one half, so rounding recovers the exact integer coefficients and carrying gives the exact binary product.

reason: Answered with moderate confidence. The overall chain (digit split, wrap-around product, reindexing to prime axes, transforms with pointwise product, rescale, round, carry) is supported by the Pegapev, Lekavon, Lolazad, Totipuv, Tobifup, Divasov, Nizizag and Nutipib pages. Two parts I took on the page's word without being able to see why they hold: the Sikusup resampling identity, and why the convolution length must be a product of odd primes. The exactness bound is stated only for digit widths of at least 2^24. I opened 10 of the 15 allowed pages: home, siz, fam, kur, mes, vub, guf, roz, pap, zom.
